title: Russell Crowe responds to Oiler Devon Levi’s ‘Gladiator’ ritual with ‘Strength and Honour’
content:
Edmonton Oilers goaltender Devon Levi’s unconventional crease routine has caught the attention of the actor who inspired it.

On Sunday morning, Russell Crowe reposted Levi’s postgame interview from Saturday night on X, responding to the 24-year-old netminder after Levi revealed his midgame ritual is based on Crowe’s character in Ridley Scott’s 2000 film “Gladiator.”

“Strength and Honour young man,” Crowe wrote, quoting his role as Roman general Maximus Decimus Meridius. His profile photo is also from the movie.

Levi backstopped the Oilers to a 1-0 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs at Scotiabank Arena on Saturday, turning aside all 19 shots he faced to record his first career NHL shutout.

During television timeouts, cameras caught Levi slipping off his blocker and pressing his bare hand flat against the ice — a move reminiscent of Maximus rubbing the dirt of the Colosseum floor between his fingers before battle.

“If I’m being honest, there’s a scene in ‘Gladiator’ where he picks up the sand and plays with it,” Levi told Sportsnet’s Kyle Bukauskas after the win. “I’ve always liked that. It’s always connected with me.”

Trading Roman sand for Canadian ice, the ritual helps Levi centre himself amid the chaos of an NHL game.

“Just a little ritual to connect with the ice,” he explained. “It locks me in. I like the feeling of the cold.”

Playing in front of 19,000 fans in Toronto to kick off Edmonton’s six-game road trip, Levi stood tall behind a tight-checking Oilers defence to secure the milestone win.

“Super special,” Levi told reporters afterward. “Since I was a kid, I’ve been thinking about getting a shutout in the NHL.”

With the victory, Levi improved to 9-1-0 this season with a 2.48 goals-against average and a .906 save percentage. Excluding a rocky Oilers debut, his save percentage sits at .926. While he didn’t face a heavy volume of shots against the Maple Leafs, he delivered several timely stops to preserve the one-goal lead.

“I’ve had some good goalies, and they’re confident,” Oilers head coach Mike Babcock said. “The situation never seems to be too big for them, and they enjoy those moments. I think that’s what you want as an athlete. Under the most heat, you want to enjoy it the most, and he seems to have good joy when he’s playing.”

Levi’s teammates echoed that sentiment, praising his competitiveness since arriving at training camp as a trade acquisition from the Buffalo Sabres.

“He just works his bag off,” forward Ryan Nugent-Hopkins said. “He’s super talented too, but it’s how competitive he is. It’s fun to watch. He deserved that one tonight.

“He’s a hell of a goalie. We saw that the second he came to camp. You’d try to shoot on him and you can’t beat him. He reads everything so well. He wants to be in these tight games, and he wants to give us a chance every night. For him to have that talent and also that competitiveness is impressive.”

The Oilers continue their Eastern road swing Sunday night when they visit the Philadelphia Flyers at Xfinity Mobile Arena.
